properties.statement:
THE REMAINING ~7s OF loop_status-AFTER-A-WRITE IS DISTRIBUTED INTRINSIC GRAPH ANALYSIS, NOT A HOT SPOT — THERE IS NO CHEAP LEVER LEFT. Release phase-probes, live-store copy (3,700 nodes / 18,100 edges), load ~1.9, 2026-09-05. loop_status after a write: 7,085 ms total.

ACCOUNTED, release, by probe:
  open_defects / all_defects: 3,454 ms, itself SPREAD across six sub-detectors, none dominant:
    node_type_index 230 | parked_nodes 404 | dangling-ref scan 329 | orphan-artifact 118 |
    zero-degree scan 457 | edge loops (CONTRADICTS/DUPLICATES/ANTICIPATES) 510 | detect_structural_defects 1,406
    (detect_structural_defects itself = design_network build + operational_network + circular_dependencies + clusters, each a fraction)
  the other ~3,600 ms is loop_status_for's OWN work: open_questions (detect_gaps cold after a write + a pass over 57 Question nodes), scan_nodes(DECISION) with an outgoing() per decision for assigned-decisions (~232 store scans), the answered-question ANSWERS scans, plus count_all_nodes, the verifications digest and the record_moved sync check.

⭐ THE SHAPE: loop_status after a write runs ~FIVE independent full-or-partial graph analyses (defects across 6 detectors, gaps, questions, assigned decisions, verifications), each doing per-node or per-edge STORE READS, and a write correctly invalidates all of it so all of it recomputes. The cost is the sum of many ~0.3-1.4s pieces, not one ~5s piece. This is why the one-pass edge read (fact:the-one-pass-edge-read-is-correct-but-does-not-move-the-defect-scan-hypothesis-falsified) moved nothing: it fixed one 0.4s piece.

🛑 SO THERE ARE ONLY TWO WAYS TO MOVE IT, AND BOTH ARE ANTHONY'S CALL, NOT A LEVER I CAN PULL:
  (A) A PRODUCT TRADEOFF. loop_status need not compute everything on every call. It could report defect/gap COUNTS from a per-generation memo refreshed lazily, or say 'defects: not recomputed since last write — run detect_defects' rather than scanning. This trades completeness-on-every-call for speed, and completeness-on-every-call is a property the loop was deliberately built to have (dec:loop-status-state-not-history). Only the owner can decide that trade.
  (B) A STORE-LEVEL REFACTOR. The common thread is per-node get_node/outgoing/incoming and per-type scan_nodes across every detector. Loading ONE node+edge snapshot per write generation and having all detectors read it, instead of each hitting the store, would cut the shared substrate — but that is a large change touching every detector, it reintroduces the cache-is-a-global concern at scale, and the one-pass experiment already showed edge-gathering alone is not the bulk, so the snapshot would have to cover node reads and the algorithms too. Its size needs to be seen before it is started.

⭐ THE HONEST BOTTOM LINE, per the optimize skill's step 1 ('nothing here is worth optimising is a real and frequent answer'): the redundancy is gone. The multiplier — loop_status recomputed on every read after every write, 9.5x/session — was the redundancy, and it is fixed and merged (#428). What remains is the intrinsic cost of analysing a 3,700-node graph once per orientation after writes: ~7s, paid roughly once per orientation rather than 9.5x/session. There is no further redundancy to remove cheaply; the remaining moves cost either completeness or a large refactor.

BOUNDS: one machine, 4 cores, release, stdio, live-store copy, load ~1.9; single-run phase probes (the SPLIT is robust to noise even if each number carries ±20%). detect_defects adds sweep_scope on top of all_defects; loop_status uses open_defects (all_defects) without sweep_scope.
